scope.requirements:
# Clean design specification
Ethereum NFT raffle; immutable factory, ERC-1167 clones with immutable implementation. One entry costs 1,000,000 units of canonical six-decimal USDC. One purchase mints a transferable ERC721 ticket representing a contiguous inclusive range. Exactly one ERC721 prize is escrowed atomically at creation. Reserve met awards NFT and 95% sponsor / 5% treasury. Reserve missed awards 80% gross to winner, 15% sponsor, 5% treasury. Refund outcome pays 100% per entry and returns prize. Rounding is floor on aggregate protocol fee; remainder must be allocated without loss. No administrator, mutable configuration or upgrade. Request window [sale end, end+2days); callback accepted strictly before request timestamp+2days. Refunds open at deadline. Callback records result only. Settlement is permissionless, storage-only; redemption requires current ticket owner, burns claim atomically, and must revert all effects on delivery failure. Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement. Never move assets between raffle clones. Quote token and Chainlink wrapper are trusted canonical dependencies; arbitrary prize contracts and ticket recipients are untrusted. Frontend discovery is advisory; transaction decisions must reread current chain state.

This specification was composed before scanner results and historical findings. Source, not design prose, determines actual behavior. No tests, audit history, accepted-risk lists or scanner results are provided.

properties.reasoning: Implementation locked; factory immutable in implementation bytecode; only factory can initialize a clone once. Constructor guard zero state on clones remains safe because only ENTERED is prohibited.
Receiver requires expected token, ID, sponsor and factory operator, then factory checks reported ownership and Active status. Semantic ownership depends on prize honesty.

properties.property: Entry price, bounds and ticket ranges
properties.reasoning: Positive entries, checked uint128 aggregate, range [oldTotal+1,newTotal], one ticket per purchase. ticketCount <= totalEntries, so its increment cannot overflow earlier. USDC total <= (2^128-1)*10^6, within uint256.

Pot moves to refunds or split liabilities. Protocol=floor(gross*500/10000); cash=floor(gross*8000/10000); sponsor=remainder. Fixed one-million entry units make both shares exact for normal pots. Claims zero/decrement liabilities before transfers; reverts restore all effects.
Buy excludes end; request includes end, excludes end+2days, and requires sold entries. Caller covers actual native fee, excess refund failure reverts atomically. No USDC pot is spent for VRF.

Only immutable wrapper can call; in-flight, wrong state/id/word count and late callbacks ignored. One-based modulo selection stays within sold range; terminal status prevents repeats. Tiny modulo bias is not promoted to a material candidate.

Sold Active waits end+2days; Drawing waits request+2days; equal deadline enables refunds and excludes callback. Empty raffle sponsor may cancel early; others after sale end. Refund batch 1..100, owner-only, burn prevents duplicate claims.

Range validation and liability allocation have no external call/ownership read. Unminted [0,0] range cannot contain positive winning entry. Historical burned ranges cannot produce terminal winner claims because refund and win states are exclusive.

OwnerOf is read at claim time; approved operator alone cannot redeem. Burn and winner/prize flags revert if delivery reverts or reported ownership fails. Arbitrary token lying about owner remains a trust limitation.

Permissionless fixed-recipient quote claims are independent after settlement. Winner-delivery failure does not block separately settled quote allocations. Blocking USDC state is an external liveness assumption.
Existing same-factory plumbing is excluded. NFT sponsor return omits runtime destination screening, so a recipient that later becomes a clone can receive another raffle prize. See C01.

Core economic functions use shared per-clone guard. Factory has separate guard. Mint recipient sees already-recorded range and pot. ERC721 transfers may reenter callbacks but do not themselves change raffle liabilities; only-owner burn paths and core guards constrain economic calls.
